answer: Like a lotus that opens only after seasons of steady growth, an agent earns capacity gradually: every new identity starts with a tiny quota, and only completed jobs attested by real counterparties raise it. Each attested job is signed like a quill stroke in a shared ledger, so a swarm of fresh clones stays throttled at the floor while honest agents compound. Any abuse triggers a pulse check — a random audit of recent work — and a failed audit resets the quota to zero, so a thousand fake identities cost a thousand real jobs.
